en: The Sūtra on the Three Turnings of the Wheel of Dharma Spoken by the Buddha, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing by Imperial Command.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavat was staying at Vārāṇasī in the Deer Park of the Ṛṣipatana.
While staying in the Deer Park, the Blessed One then addressed the five bhikṣus, saying:
"O bhikṣus! You bhikṣus!"
"This is the noble truth of suffering; through appropriate attention toward the teachings as they have been heard, it gives rise to vision, knowledge, clarity, and awakening. O bhikṣus!

These dharmas—the noble truths of the origin of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the path leading to the cessation of suffering—when attended to appropriately, give rise to vision, knowledge, clarity, and awakening."

"O bhikṣus! This noble truth of suffering is a dharma to be fully understood; it should be known thus. By attending appropriately to the teachings as they have been heard, one can give rise to vision, knowledge, clarity, and awakening."

“O bhikṣus! This noble truth of the origin of suffering is a dharma to be fully understood; it should be abandoned in this way. By attending appropriately to the dharma as it has been heard, one can give rise to vision, knowledge, clarity, and awakening.”

“O bhikṣus! This noble truth of the cessation of suffering is a dharma to be fully understood; it should be realized in this way. By applying correct attention to the teachings as they have been heard, one can give rise to vision, knowledge, clarity, and awakening.”

"O bhikṣus! This noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering is a dharma that must be fully understood; it should be cultivated in this way. By attending appropriately to the teachings as they have been heard, one can give rise to vision, knowledge, clarity, and awakening."

"O bhikṣus! This noble truth of suffering is a dharma to be fully understood; having thus known it, by attending appropriately to the teachings as they have been heard, one can give rise to vision, knowledge, clarity, and awakening."

"O bhikṣus! This noble truth of the origin of suffering is a dharma to be fully understood; having thus abandoned it, through proper attention to the teachings as they have been heard, one can give rise to vision, knowledge, clarity, and awakening."

“O bhikṣus! This noble truth of the cessation of suffering is a dharma to be fully understood; having thus realized it, through proper attention to the teachings as they have been heard, one is able to give rise to vision, knowledge, clarity, and awakening.”

"O bhikṣus! This noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering is a dharma to be fully understood; having thus cultivated it, by attending appropriately to the teachings as they have been heard, one can give rise to vision, knowledge, illumination, and awakening."

“O bhikṣus! If I had not fully realized these four noble truths through their three turnings and twelve aspects, then vision, knowledge, clarity, and awakening would not have arisen within me. In that case, I would not have attained liberation of mind through the abandonment of afflictions amidst this world with its gods, Māras, Brahmās, śramaṇas, and brāhmaṇas; nor could I have realized unsurpassed bodhi.”

“O bhikṣus! Because I have fully understood these four noble truths through their three turnings and twelve aspects, vision, knowledge, clarity, and awakening have all arisen within me. Thus, amidst this entire world with its gods, Māras, Brahmās, śramaṇas, and brāhmaṇas, I have abandoned the afflictions and attained liberation of mind, whereby I was able to realize unsurpassed bodhi.”
When the Blessed One had spoken this Dharma, the Venerable Kauṇḍinya and eighty thousand devas were freed from dust and defilement, attaining the pure Dharma-eye.
The Buddha said to Kauṇḍinya,
"Do you understand this Dharma? He replied:
“I have understood,
World-Honored One!
“Have you understood this Dharma?”
He replied: "I have understood, Sugata!"
Because Kauṇḍinya had understood the Dharma, he was therefore named Ājñātakauṇḍinya; *ājñāta* means "understood.
At that time, the terrestrial yakṣas, having heard what the Buddha said, raised a great voice and proclaimed to humans and devas:

"Virtuous ones, you should know that the Buddha, staying at the Deer Park in the Abode of the Sages near Vārāṇasī, has extensively turned the Wheel of Dharma with its three revolutions and twelve aspects. By this, he brings great benefit to the entire world—including gods, humans, Māras, Brahmās, śramaṇas, and brāhmaṇas—and causes his fellow practitioners of the holy life to swiftly reach the state of secure nirvāṇa. Thus, humans and devas increase while asuras decrease."
When that yakṣa had spoken thus, all the devas in the void and the hosts of the Four Great Kings heard and knew it.

In this manner, it was transmitted in an instant throughout the six heavens of the desire realm; in a mere moment, its resonance reached as far as the Brahmā heaven. Having heard it, the assembly of Brahmās likewise proclaimed it everywhere, explaining it at length as before. For this reason, this sūtra is named "The Turning of the Wheel of Dharma for the Third Time."
At that time, the five bhikṣus, as well as the humans and devas, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
*The Sūtra on the Turning of the Wheel of Dharma Spoken by the Buddha*.
